data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Benoni means 'son of my pain'. This name holds biblical significance as the name given to the son of Jacob who was born during his struggle with the angel. Parents who choose Benoni usually hope their child will grow to embody son of my pain and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.long_meaning: Benoni, meaning son of my sorrow or son of pain, is a Biblical name that signifies the son of Rachel, who was born in Bethlehem, as written in Genesis, and who was named by his mother as a symbol of her pain and suffering during childbirth

data.cultural_impact: The name Benoni holds cultural significance in the Jewish tradition as it is derived from the Hebrew language. It serves as a reminder of the struggles and challenges that accompany the birth and raising of a child.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, the name Benoni represents the idea of bearing children through trials and tribulations. It reflects the belief that even in the midst of pain, God is present and can bring new life into the world. For Christians, this name can also be seen as a reminder of the suffering and sacrifice of Jesus Christ, who is the ultimate source of comfort and strength in times of hardship.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Benoni is a Hebrew name meaning "son of my sorrow" or "son of my pain." It is believed to be a name given to a child born to a grieving mother, symbolizing the hope and comfort found in new life amidst suffering.

biblical_reference.note: Benoni is the original name given by Rachel to her son, later changed to Benjamin by his father Jacob

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, Benoni is believed to be the original name of King Saul's son, Ish-bosheth, who reigned over Israel after Saul's death. According to the text, Benoni means 'son of my sorrow'. This name is mentioned in 2 Samuel 2:8-9 and 1 Samuel 4:2. This event occurred around 1025-1010 BC.

Benoni was also the name of a son born to Joseph and Asenath in Egypt around the time of the Israelite sojourn in Egypt. This is recorded in Genesis 41:50 and is described as a source of comfort to his father during a time of great famine. This event occurred around 1700 BC.
